finding: lr 1e-4 + alpha=rank SLOWS the damage but does not change its nature: at step 200 macro-WER matches base (0.564 vs 0.569) with pulaar/ewe improving and french/kinyarwanda held, but the interference signature re-emerges by step 600 and the strong languages erode steadily. A single shared rank-16 adapter across 9 languages is structurally interference-bound at ANY safe learning rate.

strategic_read: french (14.3%), swahili (13.7%), lingala (17.4%) already meet their absolute bars with the BASE model — they never needed training; base serves them.

The six languages below bar (kinyarwanda, wolof, fula, pulaar, ewe, yemba) should each get a PER-LANGUAGE adapter: zero interference by construction, matches the registry's per-language artifact design and the per-language T6 gate.
